stated: Reform UK will introduce a new police leadership and recruitment regime with a strong preference for ex-military officers, high standards of fitness and presentation, and the power to sack Chief Constables who allow 'two-tier policing.' They will also de-politicise the College of Policing, replace degree-standard entry with an entrance exam, require a 2-year probationary period, and implement stricter entry requirements.

source.quote: New Police Leadership and Recruitment Regime Strong preference for ex-military officers and personnel. High standards of fitness and presentation for front line officers. Sack Chief Constables that allow two-tier policing. De-Politicise the College of Policing Prioritise crime prevention, discipline, public service and high standards of strength and fitness among trainees. Replace degree-standard entry with an entrance exam. Require officers to complete a 2-year probationary period. Stricter entry requirements.

bearing_set.reason: Directly reforms police recruitment standards, leadership accountability, and entry criteria — all of which bear on policing effectiveness, crime response, and public safety, which is the core of O5.

The explicit mechanism of sacking Chief Constables who allow 'two-tier policing' directly targets equal treatment under law enforcement, an O9 indicator (equal treatment / anti-discrimination protections and due process & rule of law) — not merely a policing-efficiency question.

The 'two-tier policing' framing and any resulting cultural shift in policing directly affect police–community trust and inter-group relations, which are primary O15 indicators (social trust, sense of equal belonging).

membership_note: Three genuine bearings: the protective-good effect on policing capacity (O5), the equal-treatment enforcement mechanism (O9), and the community-trust implications of differential-treatment accountability (O15). No other fundamentals meet the non-negligible bar: the degree-to-exam switch has a marginal O4 or O14 labour-market effect too speculative to pin to a specific indicator; there is no direct new coercive power on civilians sufficient to score O10.
